title: Common definitions
description: Shapes reused across the eleven primitives. Not a primitive itself.

id.description: crest:<type>:<ULID>. Sortable by creation time, opaque to meaning.

did.description: A Party's deployment-local, pairwise DID. 'party', not 'worker': worker is a role a Party holds (§2), and an identifier that names a role cannot be reused when the same person is a supervisor.

versionedRef.description: Everything references by versioned identifier (§2). A bare id is a reference that changes meaning underneath the thing holding it.

outcome.description: A quantity of a defined activity. The unit comes from the definition, never from the source system.

sourceClass.description: What kind of system the record came from. Adapter-attached, never source-asserted (§8).

captureMethod.description: How the fact was captured at source.

provenance.description: Attached by the adapter and validated by the pipeline. Whatever the source asserts about its own trustworthiness is ignored (§8). These are the facts the strength function reads; the tier itself is never stored (§6).

adapterRef.description: Which adapter version translated the record. Resolvable in the adapter registry, so a verifier can walk evidence back to a known translator.

sourceRecordRef.description: The source system's own identifier for the record. Opaque to CREST.

sourceExposure.description: The transport a record arrived by. Recorded, and deliberately not an input to strength (§8) — an attester who could raise a tier by choosing how to send the file would have found a way to assert strength.

identityAssurance.description: Derived from a Party's identity bindings, never asserted (§4.1). Present in a computed view; never a stored field on Party.

tier.description: Never stored. Computed by the strength function at presentation time (§6). Appears only in responses.
